title: Palmitoylated proteins in bovine granulosa cells
projectDescription: The palmitoyl-proteome of bovine granulosa cells (GC) cells was investigated by combining acyl-biotin exchange chemistry and quantitative mass spectrometry analysis.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Bovine ovaries (in total, n=480) were collected at a commercial slaughterhouse. Bovine follicular cells, mainly granulosa (GC) and cumulus-oocyte complexes (COCs) were retrieved from the antral follicles 3-6 mm in diameter by aspiration. The method relies on an acyl-biotinyl exchange chemistry (ABE) reported first in 2004 (Drisdel et al. 2004) was used to purify the palmitoylated proteins according to the protocol described by Wan et al (Wan et al. 2007), which we applied with minor modifications. For identification of palmitoylated proteins, samples (HA+, HA- (control)) were fractionated by SDS-PAGE (4-20% polyacrylamide gel). Each lane was sectioned into 11 bands. After in-gel reduction (DTT), alkylation (Iodoacetamide), trypsin digestion in presence of 0.025% ProteasMax, peptides were analysed by nanoLC-MS/MS in triplicate, using a LTQ Orbitrap Velos mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Bremen, Germany) coupled to an Ultimate® 3000 RSLC Ultra High Pressure Liquid Chromatographer (Dionex, Amsterdam, The Netherlands).
dataProcessingProtocol: Mass spectrum ion searches were performed using Mascot search engine version 2.3.2 via Proteome Discoverer 2.1 software. Interrogation was made against the mammal section of the non-redundant NCBI database. The search parameters included trypsin as a protease with two allowed missed cleavages and carbamidomethylcysteine, methionine oxidation and acetylation of N-term protein as variable modifications. Peptides and proteins identified by MASCOT were subjected to Scaffold v4.8.4 software. Peptide identifications were accepted if they could be established at greater than 95% probability by the Peptide Prophet algorithm. Protein identifications were accepted if they could be established at greater than 95% probability and contained at least two unique peptides. Protein probabilities were assigned by the Protein Prophet algorithm. Proteins sharing significant peptide evidence were grouped into clusters. To characterize enriched palmitoylated proteins, +HA and –HA conditions analysed in triplicate (R1, R2, R3) with three technical replicates per bands were compared using Scaffold Q+ software (version 4.4, Proteome Software, Portland, USA). We employed a label-free quantitative approach based on Spectral Count (SC). Quantifications performed with normalized spectral counts (SC) were carried out on distinct proteins using “Weighed Spectra” option. Protein clusters were defined as enriched palmitoylated proteins if they met the following conditions: 1) detection once among the three replicates only in +HA and never in control condition –HA; 2) detection in the both conditions but with an enrichment in +HA with a fold change > 2.
